title: Conspicuity Index & Adaptive Rollback Orchestrator for Rollout Observability
creator: Priya Shah
description: Problem: teams running canary/A-B/shadow experiments in Console have to stitch together multiple views (per-route metrics, spans, token-level cost) to decide if a variant is safe. Current delta views are signal-rich but noisy; engineers often spend >2hrs debugging before reverting a bad variant. Proposal: build a Conspicuity Index — a single, explainable score that highlights how ‘noticeable’ a variant is versus baseline across multiple signal families (latency, token cost, semantic quality, hallucination markers, error rates). Pair this with an Adaptive Rollback Orchestrator (ARO) that recommends an action (hold, slow rollout, rollback, partial rollback) and can optionally automate rollback with human confirmation and staged remediation steps.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Conspicuity Index computed from at least five signal families (p50/p95 latency, per-route token cost, error-rate, semantic-metric regression from eval set, hallucination indicator) and surfaced in Console rollout detail pages. 2) Diff explainer UI shows top contributing signals and linked traces for each contribution. 3) ARO provides a ranked set of recommended actions with confidence and runbook link. 4) Manual rollback flow triggers within existing rollout APIs and creates an audit event + trace links. 5) Automated canary pause/rollback can be enabled per-project with safe-guards (2-step confirmation, dry-run).
design_notes:
- New 'Conspicuity' panel on rollout detail: single-score sparkline, contributor bar chart, cohort filter, and quick-links to traces and payload samples.
- Diff explainer will show natural-language summary: e.g., 'Variant A shows +180ms p95 in EU region and 12% higher token consumption for long prompts — top contributor: KV cache miss rate.'
- Provide color-coded severity and a hoverable distribution sampler.
- UX includes a staged rollback wizard: Suggest -> Verify -> Execute -> Postmortem.
backend_notes:
- Telemetry ingestion: extend rollout telemetry pipeline to emit normalized signal vectors per cohort/window.
- Conspicuity scoring service: weighted z-score aggregator with configurable weights per org; default weights tuned from historical regressions.
- Tracing integration: link span IDs and request IDs in contributor rows.
- ARO orchestrator: idempotent orchestration job that calls rollout APIs, writes audit events, and triggers metric guardrails.
- Data retention: keep cohort-level windows for 30 days; store samples for 7 days.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (MVP, 3 weeks): compute Conspicuity Index backend, add read-only panel in Console with links to existing cohort charts.
Phase 2 (4 weeks): diff explainer, trace linking, and ranked recommendations.
Phase 3 (2 weeks): ARO manual-trigger rollback flow and audit logging.
Phase 4 (optional, 3 weeks): opt-in automated rollback with two-step approvals and simulated dry-runs.
Pilot: onboard two internal teams (runtime and console) and one external beta customer for 6-week pilot.
Rollback safety: default to manual for pilot; automated rollback gated by customer opt-in and org-level policy.
metrics_to_monitor:
- Time-to-detect (median time from rollout start to first conspicuity alert)
- Time-to-rollback (median)
- False positive rate of ARO recommendations (after pilot)
- Post-rollback customer-facing errors (incidents)
- Adoption: % projects enabling Conspicuity panel and ARO opt-in
- Cost impact: downstream token-cost delta captured per-cohort
failure_modes:
- Noisy signals dominating index: mitigate via configurable weights and outlier-resistant aggregation.
- Missing trace linkages in high-throughput flows: fallback to sample-based linking and surface 'trace unavailable' with explanation.
- Overzealous automation causing unnecessary rollbacks: require multi-step confirmations and a simulated dry-run feature.
- Privacy/compliance concerns around payload samples: redact PII and provide KMS-backed sample storage with audit logging.
